title: Students detained in Delhi during protest against electoral roll revision

tea.why: Students are protesting against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
tea.want: The protesters are demanding the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision exercise.
tea.changed: Nov 1: Delhi Police detained at least 100 students on Minto Road while they were marching toward Connaught Place.

summary: On November 1, 2026, students organised a protest in New Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The demonstration was called by the student organisation DISHA. Participants marched from Minto Road toward Connaught Place to voice their opposition to the revision process. Delhi Police intercepted the marchers on Minto Road, preventing them from continuing their route. According to reports, at least 100 students were detained by police personnel during the action. The protest concluded after the police intervention and the subsequent detention of the participants.
demands: Cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
response: Delhi Police intercepted the marchers on Minto Road and detained at least 100 students to prevent them from proceeding toward Connaught Place.

arrests.text: At least 100 students were detained by the police

updates.text: Students marched from Minto Road toward Connaught Place to protest the electoral roll revision.
Delhi Police intercepted the protesters and detained at least 100 students.
